query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Maintaining the build plate and surrounding powder bed at an elevated, near-solidus temperature (~0.6 T_m of the alloy) throughout laser powder-bed-fusion fabrication of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy parts will simultaneously (i) cut layer-wise thermal gradients that drive warping, (ii) prolong melt-pool lifetime so that keyholes and lack-of-fusion pores heal, and (iii) suppress hot-crack initiation, thereby yielding higher dimensional precision (≈ 2× smaller geometric deviation) and improved mechanical integrity (≈ 20 % higher 0.2 % proof stress and ≈ 30 % higher uniform elongation) relative to the current room-temperature-substrate baseline.
generation.material_initial_state: Gas-atomised CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy powder (15–45 µm, spherical, ≤0.02 wt % O) processed by standard laser powder-bed fusion on a room-temperature, stainless-steel build plate in argon, giving ~2 % porosity, ±150 µm dimensional scatter and occasional hot-cracks in thin walls.
generation.intervention: Use an actively heated build platform that keeps the substrate and growing part at 0.6 T_m (≈ 600 °C for CoCrFeMnNi) during the entire additive manufacturing run.
generation.conditions: Laser power 250–300 W, scan speed 800 mm s⁻¹, hatch spacing 90 µm, layer thickness 40 µm, argon atmosphere <100 ppm O₂; component section thickness ≤10 mm; cooling to room temperature inside the chamber after build.
generation.structural_mediator: Reduced thermal gradient in each new layer enables slower solidification and enhanced diffusion, leading to (1) pore healing and higher relative density, (2) suppression of solidification cracking by lowering tensile residual stress, and (3) diminished part distortion.
generation.mechanism: At ~0.6 T_m the alloy remains solid while its yield strength is greatly reduced; this allows stress relaxation by creep during solidification and cooldown, limiting crack driving force and distortion. The hotter powder bed also lowers the temperature difference between molten pool and surroundings, lengthening melt-pool lifetime so that wetting improves and unmolten particle islands dissolve, reducing lack-of-fusion porosity. Together these effects raise density and mechanical strength, and keep build dimensions closer to the CAD model.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the room-temperature build: (a) internal porosity falls from ~2 vol % to ≤0.6 vol % (≈70 % reduction); (b) average surface-to-CAD deviation drops from ±150 µm to ±75 µm (≈50 % improvement); (c) 0.2 % proof stress rises from 750 MPa to ≥900 MPa (≈20 % gain); (d) uniform elongation increases from 14 % to ≥18 % (≈30 % gain).
generation.baseline: Standard laser powder-bed fusion of CoCrFeMnNi on an unheated plate (~25 °C), followed by build-chamber cool-down, without post-processing.
generation.boundary: Effect is expected for fcc HEAs with solidus <1500 °C; above ~0.8 T_m grain growth may over-soften the alloy and negate mechanical gains; benefits may diminish for bcc refractory HEAs whose 0.6 T_m exceeds typical PBF hardware limits, or for components thicker than ~20 mm where internal heat build-up already reduces gradients.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of improvement could vary with powder oxygen levels, evaporation of Mn at elevated temperature, and machine-specific heat-source geometry; quantitative figures are estimates requiring validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Print a set of ASTM E8 mini-tensile coupons and NIST step-gauge geometries from the same CoCrFeMnNi powder under (1) room-temperature substrate (baseline) and (2) 600 °C heated substrate (intervention) using identical scan parameters; perform no post-processing.
measurements: 3-D optical scan for dimensional deviation vs. CAD (µm RMS)
Room-temperature tensile test (0.2 % proof stress, uniform elongation)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the heated-substrate samples do NOT show (a) ≥40 % reduction in porosity OR (b) ≥20 % reduction in dimensional deviation OR (c) ≥10 % increase in both proof stress and uniform elongation, the hypothesis is falsified.
